First, we rewrite the integral as

$$
\int (9-5x)^{-3}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Let $u=9-5x.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-5\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{5}\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (9-5x)^{-3}\text{d}x & =\int {u}^{-3}\cdot (-\frac{1}{5})\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}\int {u}^{-3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}){u}^{-2}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{10{u}^{2}}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{10(9-5x)^{2}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\frac{1}{10(9-5x)^{2}}+C] & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\frac{1}{10(9-5x)^{2}}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[(9-5x)^{-2}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\cdot (-2)(9-5x)^{-3}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(9-5x)+0 \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}(9-5x)^{-3}\cdot (-5) \\  & =(9-5x)^{-3} \\  & =\frac{1}{{(9-5x)}^{3}}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
